overview.title: Your overview
overview.subtitle: Bring your records into one place. Review the details, then see the whole picture.
overview.welcomeText: A few details help us ask for the right records. You can also explore the workspace with a fictional salon.
overview.nextText: Work through the essentials at your own pace.
overview.uploadText: Add invoices, VAT submissions and bank statements.
overview.reconcileText: Record invoices and payments separately, with evidence attached.
overview.checkText: Explain the opening balances and outstanding items.
overview.previewText: See the figures built from your recorded entries.
overview.based: Based on recorded entries · before personal income tax
overview.progressText: {done} of {total} items have supporting notes. Notes still need review.
overview.empty: No entries yet. Start with your opening balances or an invoice.

business.title: Business details
business.subtitle: Your answers shape the documents and year-end information we ask for.
business.name: Business name
business.vatHelp: Set the method you actually use. The VAT check compares invoice totals for ordinary domestic quarterly returns.
business.stock: I hold products or materials in stock
business.firstYear: This is my first financial year
business.yearFixed: The year is fixed for an existing workspace. Create a new workspace for another year.
business.vatScope: Which VAT returns do you file?
business.vatScope_other: Other period, scheme or special case
business.vatScopeHelp: Choose Other for KOR, exempt or cross-border sales, reverse charge, private-use adjustments or changed methods. Check your Belastingdienst letter if unsure.

documents.title: Your documents
documents.subtitle: Keep your source records together and link them to your bookkeeping.
documents.accept: PDF, UBL XML, invoice CSV or MT940 · 20 MB per file · up to 100 PDF pages
documents.capability: Group sales and purchase invoices separately for easier review. One PDF can contain several invoices. Check the original for each draft.
documents.emptyText: Add a source file to start building an evidence trail.
documents.textNote: Lavin saves the originals and prepares drafts or movements when it recognizes the file. Review them in Bookkeeping.
documents.noText: No readable text was found. Review the original and enter the figures manually.
documents.gather: Records to collect for this year
documents.gatherHelp: Upload any available invoices, bank statements and filed VAT returns. Check Year-end checks for records specific to your business.

review.title: Bookkeeping
review.subtitle: Record the business event first, then its payment. Each entry stays balanced.
review.invoiceHelp: Use the VAT amount from the invoice. Payment is recorded separately against receivables or payables.
review.purchaseHelp: Enter only the VAT you can reclaim. Enter 0 if none is deductible. The rest stays in the expense or asset amount. Record payment separately against payables.
review.journalHelp: Choose the debit and credit accounts. For corrections, add a reversing entry and explain the change.
review.bankHelp: Choose the other account before recording a movement. To settle a recorded invoice, use receivables or payables. Use VAT check to compare booked invoice VAT with the filed return.
review.noBank: Upload an MT940 or a text-based bank PDF to review bank movements here.
review.amountHelp: Enter amounts without thousands separators. Use a point or comma for decimals, such as 121.50 or 121,50. Reverse the debit and credit accounts for negative corrections.

yearend.title: Year-end checks
yearend.subtitle: Capture the explanations and supporting details your reviewer will need.
yearend.notice: Saving notes marks an item as supplied, not verified. Automated schedule calculations and accountant sign-off are coming in a later milestone.
yearend.placeholder: Describe the balance, period and supporting documents…
yearend.openingHelp: Explain the opening position and how it agrees with last year. For a new business, confirm the starting capital and assets.
yearend.bankHelp: Confirm all accounts and periods are covered, and reconcile opening and closing balances.
yearend.salesHelp: Confirm invoices, refunds and cash/card sales are complete without double counting.
yearend.purchasesHelp: Confirm supplier invoices and business receipts are complete, including personally paid costs.
yearend.vatHelp: Compare your filed returns with the books. Use a note to explain differences, corrections, payments and any VAT still outstanding at year end.
yearend.ownerHelp: Explain private transfers and distinguish them from revenue and expenses.
yearend.cutoffHelp: List unpaid invoices, accruals and prepaid expenses, including bills arriving after year-end.
yearend.comparativesHelp: Provide prior-year accounts and details supporting the opening balances. Comparative reporting is not implemented yet.
yearend.cashHelp: Provide the year-end cash count and explain its reconciliation to the cashbook.
yearend.stockHelp: List quantities, purchase costs and obsolete stock at year-end.
yearend.equipmentHelp: Provide historical costs, accumulated depreciation, additions, disposals and useful lives.
yearend.premisesHelp: Identify lease commitments, refundable deposits and payments covering future periods.
yearend.staffHelp: Provide reviewed payroll summaries and outstanding payroll obligations. No payroll is calculated here.
yearend.loansHelp: Reconcile opening principal, advances, repayments, interest and closing principal.

report.title: Annual report
report.subtitle: A draft overview calculated directly from your journal. No figures are invented or estimated.
report.readiness: Before this becomes a reviewed report
report.noEntries: Record the opening position and business transactions.
report.evidence: Complete the outstanding evidence notes and have them reviewed.
report.draftOnly: Complete the year-end checks and have the figures reviewed. This report is a draft.
report.basis: Draft management overview for a Dutch sole proprietor, based solely on recorded entries. It is not a filed tax return or an accountant’s assurance statement.
report.empty: Record an entry to populate this report.
report.reportNote: Unrecorded items, VAT timing adjustments and incomplete evidence can change these figures. Review the underlying journal before relying on this overview.
report.vatReview: Review the VAT comparison and explain any differences.

auth.shared: Shared preview. Everyone invited can view and change the same records.

guide.title: Your first report, step by step
guide.intro: From Home, choose Start a new report or Open an existing report. Then follow these five steps. Your saved records are kept until you choose to open them.
guide.quickText: Follow the short guide from your first upload to a draft report.
guide.help: What do I do on this page?

business.title: Set up your business
business.text: From Home, choose Start a new report. Enter the company name, year and activity, then select Next: your records. Choose the relevant features and select Create report and add documents. To revise a saved company, choose Edit company information on Home.
business.tip: Not sure about the VAT method? Choose “Not sure yet” and ask your accountant. The reporting year cannot be changed after creating this workspace.

documents.title: Upload your records
documents.text: On Documents, choose a document type and select the available files together. Upload PDF invoices and bundles, UBL XML, invoice CSV, filed VAT PDFs, and MT940 or searchable bank statements.
documents.tip: Check the status beside each file. Open an upload to change its category or delete it before posting. Use Bookkeeping to review invoice drafts and bank movements. Link filed VAT returns using the quarter links.

review.title: Record invoices and payments
review.text: Enter your opening balances. Open the invoice drafts in Bookkeeping to check the date and amounts against the originals. Confirm deductible VAT and the account for purchases. Use manual entry for any remaining invoices or corrections.
review.tip: Review imported bank movements separately. For payment of an invoice already recorded, choose Trade receivables for a customer or Trade payables for a supplier. This avoids counting income or costs twice.

yearend.title: Complete the year-end checks
yearend.text: Work through the checklist. For each item, explain the balance and name the documents that support it, then save your note. Include unpaid invoices and private transfers.
yearend.tip: A saved note means information was supplied. It still needs checking, and does not change the figures in your report.

report.title: Review and save your draft
report.text: Check the outstanding items and totals. Choose English or Dutch for the report. Select Print / save PDF, then choose Save as PDF in your browser. Use Export journal CSV to share the entries.
report.tip: Ask your accountant to check the draft before using it. VAT reconciliation and tax filing are not automatic, and this app does not submit anything to the tax authority.

guide.prepareText: Invoices and receipts, VAT returns, complete bank statements, previous closing balances (or your starting capital), and details of unpaid bills, assets and loans.
guide.exampleText: You invoice a customer €121, including €21 VAT. Record a sales invoice for 121.00 and VAT of 21.00. When €121 arrives in your bank, record it against Trade receivables. Revenue stays €100.
guide.openingText: What the business owned and owed at the start of the year.

vat.title: Quarterly VAT check
vat.subtitle: Compare VAT recorded on invoices with the figures from an original filed return.
vat.rounding: Journal amounts are grouped by booking date and kept in cents. The filed return uses whole euros. Check the period and compare differences with the original return.
vat.scopeHelp: The difference is available for ordinary quarterly domestic VAT under the invoice method. Cash accounting, other periods and special cases need a separate review.
vat.noInvoices: There are no included invoices for this quarter. Confirm whether this was a nil period or whether records are missing.

vat.captureHelp: Select the original filed PDF for this company and quarter and copy 5a and 5b as signed whole euros. Confirm invoice timing and deductible VAT against your records. Upload corrections separately and explain them in the note.
